inShort: B plays balls like a return, and A answers each one from the baseline with a soft drop into the kitchen. 15 balls, then swap.
rules: A stands behind the baseline. B stands at the kitchen line on the other side and starts every ball: a flat, medium-deep ball, like a return.
B mixes where the balls go: to A's forehand, backhand and middle, in a set order (for example forehand, backhand, forehand).
A moves the feet to the ball and lets it rise and fall: hit it on the way down, after its highest point.
A plays a drop cross-court or to the middle: about 45 cm over the net, landing in the kitchen close to B's feet.
After each ball, A notes silently: good, too high, or into the net. B says nothing.
tooEasy: B plays at real return pace and adds topspin to some balls, which are harder to read. A counts good drops in a row: 5, then 10, then 15.
tooHard: B plays slow, medium balls, always to the same spot.
goodLooksLike: About 12 of 15 drops are good: low over the net and landing in the kitchen.
